## Preliminaries

**Working scope (declared as assumption, not fact).** Hos 3:1-5 is taken as a single reading unit: a second, explicit sign-act commission, this time textually compared to the LORD's own love (v1) → [v2 missing, see insufficiencies] → Hosea's own quoted words imposing a period of exclusive seclusion on the woman, with a matching reciprocal restraint of his own (v3) → the sign's stated national meaning: Israel's own coming period of stripped political/cultic deprivation (v4) → a final, positive resolution: Israel's own future genuine return and seeking (v5). "Bearing on the inner being": (i) Hosea himself, given, for the first time in this book, his own directly-quoted first-person speech (v3) and his own commanded love, EXPLICITLY compared to the LORD's own stated love (v1); (ii) the woman ("a woman... an adulteress" — traditionally identified with Gomer, though this chapter's own surviving text does not use her name), given a stated required behaviour but, as throughout, no stated interior of her own; (iii) the LORD, both the commissioning voice (v1) and the explicit referent of the comparison within that same verse; (iv) the children of Israel, twice named as a collective (vv4-5), first deprived, then genuinely returning.

**Reading rule applied.** No [AMBIGUOUS]-span STEP-live resolution was needed — the base extract reports 100% meaning coverage for this range (61/61 non-particle spans). Register: first-person divine command with an embedded simile (v1); narrated first-person report of Hosea's own speech (v3); third-person prophetic description of Israel's future deprivation (v4) and future restoration (v5).

## Per-verse debate

### Hos 3:1

> And the Lord said to me, “ Go again, love a woman who is loved by another man and is an adulteress, even as the Lord loves the children of Israel, though they turn to other gods and love cakes of raisins.”

**Observation.** "And the LORD [H3068G] said [H0559] to me, 'Go [H1980G] again [H5750/H0413/H9030], love [H0157G] a woman [H0802G] who is loved [H0157G] by another man [H7453] and is an adulteress [H5003], even as the LORD [H3068G] loves [H0157G] the children [H1121G/H0853] of Israel [H3478], though they [H1992] turn [H6437G/H9002] to other [H0312] gods [H0430J/H0413] and love [H0160/H9004] cakes [H0809] of raisins [H6025].'"

**Operation 1 — the LORD's own renewed command to Hosea, this time EXPLICITLY compared to the LORD's own stated love for Israel.**
- **Action-type:** commanded/compared — a sign-act commission (as in ch1:2) but here, uniquely, with the comparison stated directly and explicitly within the command itself, not left implicit or inferred.
- **Subject:** Hosea, commanded; the LORD, both commanding and the explicit standard of comparison ("even as the LORD loves...").
- **Operation:** a movement — a renewed command ("go AGAIN"), its content (loving an unfaithful woman) directly likened, within the verse's own words, to the LORD's own stated disposition toward unfaithful Israel.
- **Source:** the LORD, both the command's source and the compared party.
- **Target:** the woman (Hosea's commanded object); the children of Israel (the LORD's own compared object).

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Hosea, commanded; the woman, given a stated status (loved by another, an adulteress) but no interior; the children of Israel, given a stated collective disposition ("turn to other gods, love raisin cakes" — cultic language, likely idolatrous ritual food, referential).
- Q3: Stated explicitly — this is the verse's own defining feature: the comparison is not inferred or constructed by the reader but given directly in the text's own words ("even as").
- Q4: Source of the command to Hosea = the LORD; source of Israel's own turning to other gods = themselves, explicit ("they turn").
- Q5: Target of Hosea's command = the woman; target of Israel's own turning = "other gods."
- Q6: Movement throughout.
- Q7/Q12: **This book's first EXPLICIT, textually-anchored Q12 instance — the clearest possible case, since the comparison is not merely juxtaposed but directly stated in the verse's own grammar ("even as").** Hosea's own commanded operation (loving an unfaithful woman) is directly and explicitly likened to the LORD's own stated operation (loving unfaithful Israel) — resolving EQ1 (carried from ch1-2): Q12 as currently scoped (a textually-anchored comparison between a human and a divine operation) DOES capture this instance perfectly; the earlier difficulty (ch1-2) was that the mirroring there was structural/whole-chapter, without a single verse making the comparison explicit — here, for the first time, the text does exactly that, in one clause. Both the earlier structural instances and this explicit one are now understood as belonging to the same device, operating at different levels of directness (see emergent questions).
- Q8: "The children of Israel," a collective, the LORD's own compared object.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; "cakes of raisins" is named as likely referring to some cultic/ritual food practice (referential), not elaborated within this base extract.
- Q11: commanded/compared.

**Decision.** Retain. Flagged as the book's clearest, most explicit Q12 (divine-mirroring) instance so far — directly resolving EQ1.

**Verse gap -- by design.** `Hosea 3:2` has no verse row in iba.db (no onboarded term's concordance search ever surfaced it -- see governance.verse_gap_by_design). Not an error; continuing with the next available verse. **Note beyond the standard gap notice:** the missing verse is the narrated purchase-price ("So I bought her for fifteen shekels of silver and a homer and a lethech of barley") — a further instance, after ch1:3's missing compliance-verse, of the book's own narrated FULFILMENT of a command being the specific part missing from this base extract, while the command itself (v1) and its aftermath (v3) both survive.

### Hos 3:3

> And I said to her, “You must dwell as mine for many days. You shall not play the whore, or belong to another man; so will I also be to you.”

**Observation.** "And I said [H0559] to her, 'You must dwell [H3427] as mine for many [H7227A] days [H3117G/H9034]. You shall not [H3808] play the whore [H2181/H9005/H9030], or belong [H1961/H3808/H9002] to another man [H0376G/H9005]; so [H1571/H9002] will I [H0589] also [to] [H0413/H0413] you [H9032].'"

**Operation 1 — Hosea's own quoted words, imposing seclusion on the woman AND a matching reciprocal restraint on himself.**
- **Action-type:** instructed/committed — the first time in this book Hosea himself, not only the LORD, is given a directly-quoted first-person speech-act.
- **Subject:** Hosea, self, now the operation's own source, not merely its addressee.
- **Operation:** a state/movement — a stated condition imposed on the woman (extended seclusion, sexual exclusivity), paired with a stated matching commitment from Hosea himself ("so will I also be to you") — a genuinely reciprocal structure, not a one-sided demand.
- **Source:** Hosea, self, both halves of the reciprocal commitment.
- **Target:** the woman, addressed directly.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Hosea, given his own stated interior act (a spoken commitment) for the first time in this book — a significant shift from being purely the command's recipient (ch1-2) to being, himself, an operative party with his own speech and commitment.
- Q3: Stated explicitly, as direct quotation.
- Q4: Source = Hosea, self, both the condition imposed on her and his own matching restraint.
- Q5: Target = the woman.
- Q6: State (the imposed condition) and movement (the enacted seclusion).
- Q7: Direct linkage forward to v4 (the identical phrase "dwell... many days" applied next to the whole nation) — a deliberate structural parallel between the woman's own individual sign-period and Israel's own coming national deprivation-period.
- Q8: N/A directly — an individual address.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; the woman's own reaction or compliance is not recorded (a further silence, consistent with ch1-2's pattern).
- Q11: instructed/committed.

**Decision.** Retain. Flagged as Hosea's own first directly-quoted operative act in this book, and the direct lexical anchor for v4's national parallel.

### Hos 3:4

> For the children of Israel shall dwell many days without king or prince, without sacrifice or pillar, without ephod or household gods.

**Observation.** "For the children [H1121G] of Israel [H3478] shall dwell [H3427] many [H7227A] days [H3117G/H3588A] without [H0369] king [H4428G] or prince [H8269], without [H0369/H9002] sacrifice [H2077] or pillar [H4676/H0369/H9002], without [H0369/H9002] ephod [H0646/H0369/H9002] or household gods [H8655/H9002]."

**Operation 1 — Israel's own stated future deprivation: a comprehensive stripping of political and cultic structure.**
- **Action-type:** deprived/stripped (a listed, comprehensive removal, both LEGITIMATE institutions — king, sacrifice, ephod — and illegitimate ones — pillar, household gods/teraphim — grouped together without distinction).
- **Subject:** "the children of Israel," a collective (Q8).
- **Operation:** a state — a stated future condition, directly using the same verb/phrase as v3 ("dwell... many days"), applied now to the whole nation.
- **Source:** unstated directly within this verse (passive/stative construction); by continuation of the book's pattern, the LORD's own judgment.
- **Target:** the nation's own political (king, prince) and cultic (sacrifice, pillar, ephod, household gods) apparatus, comprehensively removed.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: The nation, a collective, given a stated future condition directly paralleling the woman's own individual seclusion (v3).
- Q3: Stated explicitly, as a list.
- Q4: Source not explicitly restated within this verse (passive), continuing the book's established pattern of the LORD as ultimate source.
- Q5: Target = the nation's own institutional apparatus, both legitimate and illegitimate items grouped together without distinction — worth flagging: this verse does not separate "good" institutions (king, sacrifice, ephod — parts of the LORD's own prescribed order) from "bad" ones (pillar, teraphim — idolatrous) in its listing, an ambiguity similar to ch2:11's undifferentiated festival-termination.
- Q6: State — a comprehensive stripped condition.
- Q7: **Direct lexical linkage to v3** — "dwell... many days," applied there to the woman's individual seclusion, now to the whole nation's period of deprivation — the chapter's clearest structural parallel between the individual sign-act and its national meaning.
- Q8: The whole nation, a collective, its institutional life entirely suspended.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; whether the grouping of legitimate and illegitimate institutions together is deliberate (a total suspension regardless of origin, as at ch2:11) or simply descriptive of the historical deprivation is not resolved by this verse — named, not decided.
- Q11: deprived/stripped.

**Decision.** Retain. Flagged as the direct lexical/structural parallel to v3, and a further instance (after ch2:11) of an undifferentiated legitimate/illegitimate institutional listing.

### Hos 3:5

> Afterward the children of Israel shall return and seek the Lord their God, and David their king, and they shall come in fear to the Lord and to his goodness in the latter days.

**Observation.** "Afterward [H0310A] the children [H1121G] of Israel [H3478] shall return [H7725G] and seek [H1245] the LORD [H3068G/H0853] their God [H0430G], and David [H1732/H9028/H0853/H9002] their king [H4428G], and they shall come in fear [H6342/H9028] to [H0413] the LORD [H3068G] and to [H0413] his goodness [H2898/H9002] in the latter [H0319/H9003/H9023] days [H3117G/H9009]."

**Operation 1 — Israel's own future, unambiguously positive act of returning and seeking.**
- **Action-type:** returned/sought (the same verb, "return," H7725G, as ch2:7,9 — but here without any stated self-interested motive, paired instead with "seek the LORD their God," "come in fear," and "to his goodness").
- **Subject:** "the children of Israel," the collective, given a genuinely positive future operation of their own, following the deprivation period (v4).
- **Operation:** a movement — a stated future return, explicitly God-ward in both its object (the LORD, "and David their king" — a referential messianic/Davidic-restoration allusion, not elaborated within this verse) and its manner ("in fear," "to his goodness").
- **Source:** self — the collective's own future act, though its enabling context is the preceding deprivation-period (v4), which the text implies as formative rather than merely punitive.
- **Target:** the LORD (sought); "David their king" (sought alongside).

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: The nation, given a genuinely positive, unambiguous future operation — directly answering EQ4 (carried from ch2): unlike ch2:7's "return," whose stated motive was bare self-interest ("better for me then than now"), this future return is explicitly qualified as seeking the LORD himself, in fear, toward his goodness — no self-interested motive is stated or implied here.
- Q3: Stated explicitly.
- Q4: Source = the nation's own future act; its ENABLEMENT (the preceding deprivation, v4) is distinguished from the disposition itself (genuine seeking), consistent with Part B.5.
- Q5: Target = the LORD and "David their king" (referential to a future Davidic hope, not elaborated here).
- Q6: Movement — return, seeking, coming.
- Q7: **Direct resolution of EQ4 (ch2:7).** The same "return" verb (H7725G) recurs a third time in this book (ch2:7, ch2:9's "take back," here) — here, uniquely, coupled with explicitly God-ward, non-self-interested content ("seek the LORD," "in fear," "to his goodness"), resolving the open question of whether this book ever depicts a genuine (not merely self-interested) human turning: it does, here, though notably only AFTER, and perhaps because of, the deprivation-period (v4) — worth carrying forward as a further nuance (does the method judge this return genuine BECAUSE of the stripping, or independently of it?).
- Q8: The nation, a collective.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; "David their king" is named as a referential, not elaborated, messianic allusion.
- Q11: returned/sought.

**Decision.** Retain. Flagged as the direct, positive resolution of EQ4 — this book's first unambiguous instance of a human return not qualified by self-interest.

## Passage-level linkages (Q7)

1. **V1's explicit Q12 instance — the book's clearest divine-mirroring anchor**, directly resolving EQ1 (carried from ch1-2): the earlier structural/whole-chapter mirroring and this verse's single-clause explicit comparison are now understood as the same device operating at different levels of directness.
2. **The "dwell... many days" phrase, shared verbatim by v3 (the woman's individual seclusion) and v4 (Israel's national deprivation)** — the chapter's clearest structural parallel between sign-act and its meaning.
3. **The "return" thread (ch2:7,9; here v5), resolving EQ4** — this book's first unambiguous, non-self-interested instance of human return, though its relationship to the preceding deprivation-period (v4) as cause or mere sequence is left open.
4. **A further undifferentiated legitimate/illegitimate institutional listing (v4), echoing ch2:11's undifferentiated festival-termination** — worth tracking as a recurring feature of this book's judgment-language.

## Insufficiencies register

1. **Hos 3:2 (the purchase-price verse) is entirely missing from iba.db** — a further instance (after ch1:3) of a command's own narrated fulfilment being specifically absent from this base extract, while the command (v1) and its aftermath (v3) survive.
2. **The woman's own reaction to Hosea's imposed condition (v3) is never stated** — a further silence, consistent with this book's recurring pattern (ch1-2) of giving the wife-figure no stated interior of her own.
3. **Whether v4's grouping of legitimate (king, sacrifice, ephod) and illegitimate (pillar, teraphim) institutions together is deliberate or merely descriptive is not resolved by this base extract.**
4. **"David their king" (v5) is named as a referential messianic/Davidic allusion; its fuller background (2 Samuel's Davidic covenant) is not part of this base extract.**

## Emergent questions log (filed against this passage — not merged across passages; resolved, if at all, at the whole-book read)

- **EQ1 — RESOLVED (carried from ch1-2).** V1 supplies this book's first explicit, single-clause Q12 instance ("even as the LORD loves the children of Israel"), confirming that Q12 as currently scoped does capture Hosea's marriage-as-mirror device when the text states the comparison directly — the earlier chapters' difficulty was that their mirroring was structural/pervasive rather than located in one verse's explicit grammar. Both modes (explicit, single-verse; structural, whole-chapter) are now understood as belonging to the same device.
- **EQ4 — substantially addressed (carried from ch2).** V5 gives this book's first unambiguous, God-ward, non-self-interested "return" — directly answering whether such a turning is ever depicted as genuine. A residual question remains: whether this genuine return is understood as CAUSED by the preceding deprivation-period (v4), or merely sequential to it — carried forward as a refinement, not a fresh open question.
- **EQ6 (new).** V4 groups legitimate institutions (king, sacrifice, ephod — the LORD's own prescribed order) and illegitimate ones (pillar, teraphim) together in a single undifferentiated list of what Israel will lack — echoing ch2:11's identical ambiguity (Sabbaths/appointed feasts vs. Baal-worship, similarly undifferentiated). Worth tracking as a recurring feature: does this book's judgment-language deliberately not distinguish corrupted-legitimate from illegitimate religious practice, or is this simply incidental to the specific historical deprivation being described?
